CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left-sided lower back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports left-sided lower back pain following microdiscectomy surgery in November 2020 for a herniated disk that was compressing the spinal thecal sac. He previously experienced severe nerve pain radiating down his leg. Currently, he has left-sided low back pain that is variable, sometimes occurring on the right side depending on the day, generally in the area where surgery was performed. Pain is worse with bending over and occurs randomly. Stretching provides relief. Pain occurs with weight-bearing while standing. He has tried ibuprofen 800 mg daily without adequate relief. Denies pain down legs currently or nerve pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current nerve pain down legs. Otherwise not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Lumbar microdiscectomy surgery in November 2020 for herniated disk compressing spinal thecal sac.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient able to bend forward without current pain. No pain with extension. Pain with weight-bearing while standing. Tenderness with palpation to left side around L5. No tenderness with palpation to right side. Normal dorsiflexion. Normal strength with foot push-back against examiner. Normal range of motion. No pain down legs.

RESULTS
X-ray of spine shows no fractures or abnormalities of spinal bone. Surgical site has healed properly.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Muscle pull from spinal misalignment. Prescribed physical therapy with VA physical therapist. Prescribed meloxicam instead of ibuprofen for improved pain management. Referral to pain management for discussion of pain management strategies and non-narcotic options. Prescribed demerol.
